prediction.likelyOutcome: Liability is locked in for CLE Venture Fund on both the note and the guaranty; the only open question is how much of a credit the borrowers get against the debt for the property's 2018 value. Because the borrowers' own valuation expert ignored a material HUD rent restriction while the lender's expert accounted for it and used a more defensible methodology for an abandoned asset, the court is more likely than not to credit a lower valuation, pushing the ultimate deficiency toward the high end of the range — likely close to (or arguably exceeding, if the court is willing to award beyond the pled demand) the originally requested $2,446,775.94, subject to appellate noise over the Exhibit C/expert-authorship rulings and to Crigler's actual collectibility.

outcome.description: After a bench trial on value the court adopted the lender's expert's retrospective value of $1,310,000 as of the March 27, 2018 transfer, credited it against the debt, and on June 14, 2024 entered judgment against the borrowers and guarantor, jointly and severally, for $1,735,579.45 plus default-rate interest (the lender later withdrew its fee request). The Eighth District affirmed.
